title: A generic-fibre basis with smaller-dimensional cokernel support
statement: Let $Y\to B$ be a smooth morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with geometrically irreducible fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of a fixed dimension $d\geq0$ [def-kun-dimension], and let $b\in B$. Let $\mathcal H$ be any finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. If $\xi$ is the generic point of $Y_b$, there exist $r\geq0$ and a module map $\alpha:\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal H$ whose induced map $\kappa(\xi)^r\to\mathcal H_\xi\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}}\kappa(\xi)$ is an isomorphism. The sheaf $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ is finite-type and quasi-coherent, and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal Q_b)$ is a proper closed subset of $Y_b$, not containing $\xi$. If this support is nonempty, its dimension, and its dimension at any of its points, is strictly less than $d$; if $d=0$ it is empty. Support is the set of nonzero stalks, cokernel is the quotient sheaf by the image, and the subscript $b$ denotes tensor pullback to $Y_b=Y\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No flatness of $\mathcal H$ over $B$ and no finite presentation of $\mathcal H$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05HF (lemma-existence-alpha), proof applied to any finite-type quasi-coherent module on its smooth target; permits r=0 when the generic fibre is zero. The proof uses only the smooth geometrically irreducible fibre of dimension d, not the rest of a devissage.

proof.text: Write $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and put $M=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H)$. The affine finite-type criterion makes $M$ finite over $R$, and the affine tilde/global-sections counit gives $\mathcal H\cong\widetilde M$. Let $p\subset R$ correspond to the image of $\xi$ in $Y$, and put $K=\kappa(p)$. The tilde stalk is $M_p$. Its residue tensor is canonically $M\otimes_RK$: the inverse maps are $(m/s)\otimes a\mapsto m\otimes a/\bar s$ and $m\otimes a\mapsto(m/1)\otimes a$, where $s\notin p$. The tensor relations verify both composites.

source.place: Tag 05HF (lemma-existence-alpha), proof: affine finite module, choice of basis images, Nakayama, and dimension drop.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating list $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ of $M$. Its images $m_i\otimes1$ span $M\otimes_RK$, by expanding the first entry of every pure tensor. Scan the list, keeping a vector precisely when it is outside the span of the previously kept vectors. The kept vectors are independent and span the original list, hence form a basis. Write their number as $r$ and their lifts as $x_1,\ldots,x_r$. The linear map $a:R^r\to M$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum c_ix_i$, becomes an isomorphism over $K$. If the tensor is zero the kept list is empty and $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 05HF (lemma-existence-alpha), proof: affine finite module, choice of basis images, Nakayama, and dimension drop.

proof.text: Use the tilde functor and the counit from step 1 to turn $a$ into $\alpha:\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal H$. Indeed the finite direct sum of $r$ copies of $\widetilde R=\mathcal O_Y$ is $\widetilde{R^r}$, since tilde preserves colimits. Naturality of the tilde stalk localization sends the germ of $x_i$ to $x_i/1$, so the residue map of $\alpha$ is exactly the basis map from step 2. Set $T=M/\operatorname{im}a$. The quasi-coherent cokernel theorem identifies $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ as quasi-coherent with affine sections $T$; the images of the $m_i$ generate $T$, and the finite-type criterion makes $\mathcal Q$ finite type.

source.place: Tag 05HF (lemma-existence-alpha), proof: affine finite module, choice of basis images, Nakayama, and dimension drop.

proof.text: Tensor the cokernel sequence $R^r\to M\to T\to0$ with $K$. Tensor right exactness and the basis isomorphism give $T\otimes_RK=0$. The same fraction formulas as in step 1 identify this with $T_p\otimes_{R_p}K$. The module $T_p$ is finite over the local ring $R_p$: the fractions $\bar m_i/1$ generate it. Apply local Nakayama to the empty generating list; its residue quotient is zero, so $T_p=0$. Thus $\mathcal Q$ has zero stalk at the image of $\xi$.

source.place: Tag 05HF (lemma-existence-alpha), proof: affine finite module, choice of basis images, Nakayama, and dimension drop.

proof.text: Write $b$ as the prime $q\subset A$ and $Y_b=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C=R\otimes_A\kappa(q)$ by the affine fibre-product formula. Let $P\subset C$ be the prime of $\xi$. Its contraction is $p$, and the fibre-ring residue theorem identifies $\kappa(P)$ with $K$, so the residue isomorphism proved above is exactly the one in the statement. The pullback stalk formula gives $(\mathcal Q_b)_\xi\cong\mathcal Q_p\otimes_{R_p}C_P=0$. Affine pullback identifies $\mathcal Q_b$ with $\widetilde{C\otimes_RT}$. The tensors $1\otimes\bar m_i$ generate $C\otimes_RT$ over $C$, so this module is finite. Its stalk support, by tilde stalk localization and the finite-module support theorem, is $Z=V(\operatorname{Ann}_C(C\otimes_RT))$, a closed subset of $Y_b$. It misses $\xi$, hence is proper.

source.place: Tag 05HF (lemma-existence-alpha), proof: affine finite module, choice of basis images, Nakayama, and dimension drop.

proof.text: Geometric irreducibility, specialized to the identity extension of $\kappa(b)$, makes $Y_b$ irreducible. Its dimension is $d$ by hypothesis. Apply the irreducible-open-complement dimension theorem with the nonempty open $U=Y_b\setminus Z$ (which contains $\xi$). It gives $Z=\varnothing$, or $\dim Z\leq e<d$ for some natural number $e$. This proves the strict global bound whenever $Z$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 05HF (lemma-existence-alpha), proof: affine finite module, choice of basis images, Nakayama, and dimension drop.

proof.text: At a point $z\in Z$ the dimension at $z$ is at most $\dim Z$: the whole space $Z$ is one of its open neighbourhoods in the defining minimum. Thus the pointwise bound follows from step 6. If $d=0$, the nonempty alternative would supply a natural number $e<0$, which is impossible, so $Z$ is empty. The argument imposed neither flatness nor finite presentation on $\mathcal H$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q29-ea5a3ec7f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First S1 split. The statement is unchanged, there are no new nodes and no SGA source; the review is in review.md. I read Stacks flat.tex 05HF (lemma-existence-alpha) in full. Its proof needs only that the affine module is finite, a basis of N⊗κ(p) that lifts to N, Nakayama for the cokernel, and that the fibre is geometrically irreducible of dimension n. The item's generalization to any finite-type quasi-coherent H with r≥0 is therefore correct. Stacks writes r>0, but its proof takes r equal to the residue dimension, which can be 0, and the citer lem-trf-complete-algebra-devissage-etale-existence uses r≥0 and d=0. I checked all 7 steps against the statements of the cited nodes. (1) The affine finite-type criterion (a) and the tilde counit (3) give H≅M̃ with M finite; the fraction formulas identify M_p⊗κ(p) with M⊗κ(p). (2) The greedy basis lifts to M; r=0 when the residue space is zero. (3) α is built from tilde, colimit preservation and the counit (R̃=O_Y is the definition, 01HV). The cokernel-image node (2)-(3) gives Q(Y)=M/im a with no Noetherian hypothesis, and the same generators make Q finite type. (4) Right exactness gives T⊗K=0, and Nakayama on the empty list over R_p gives T_p=0. (5) The fibre-product node gives C=R⊗κ(q). The fibre-ring residue node (R_p→C_P) gives κ(P)≅κ(p), so the statement's residue field is the right one. The pullback-stalk formula gives (Q_b)_ξ=0; tilde pullback and the support-annihilator node give Z=V(Ann), which is closed and proper. (6) For irreducible-open-complement-dimension I read the statement and its 2 proof steps (chain extension); topological Krull dimension agrees with def-kun-dimension on |Y_b|. (7) The pointwise bound and the d=0 case are elementary. Small cases checked: H=0; A¹ with k[x]/(x)⊕k[x] gives r=1, Z={0}; torsion H gives r=0; d=0 gives Z empty. No hypothesis is used that is not there, and the base may be non-Noetherian. Duplicate search (05HF, generic basis, proper closed dimension): lem-trf-generic-free-cokernel-dimension-drop and lem-trf-smooth-generic-rank-reduction need flatness, so neither is a duplicate. The off-unit lem-weil-pbc nodes are mathlib or slopmaster2-closed. The declared tool_use new-node-irreducible-open-complement-dimension (sec-curve-estimates) is accepted as a generic topological black box. review_split.py printed 'no such node' for every citation because it does not follow the symlinked chapters; find -L shows all 16 proof_deps and 11 stmt_deps exist. No fixes.
